notes:
Lead: Ambercliff InsightHub (product analytics platform) migrating conversational + search features from incumbent LLM provider to Redwood.

Background / ask:
- Mid-market SaaS (product teams, ~350 employees). Current stack uses OpenAI endpoints for chat, document search (reranker + embeddings) and a homegrown wrapper. Looking to reduce unit cost and gain deterministic latency for customer-facing features.
- Plan: develop on Redwood Hosted API (compat layer to preserve OpenAI payloads) -> after parity and regressions cleared, move to Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and VPC controls.

POC specifics (current):
- 4-week POC started 2026-02-03. Ingested ~15k product docs and support transcripts. Running 3 workloads in POC: embedded search (batch embeddings), reranking pipeline, and short-form summarization for in-app help.
- Targets: p95 latency <250ms for chat/generative snippets, sustained throughput ~80-100 QPS spike-safe, cost reduction goal ~30% per token compared to incumbent.
- Observed during POC: tokenization differences cause slight length drift; summarization tone/length differs causing downstream UI clipping; safety filters slightly different (one false-positive flag in support flow). SE has created a prompt-parity test harness and regression suite.

Security / compliance:
- Ambercliff requires SSO (SAML), audit logging for admin actions, KMS support for key management, and data residency controls for EU customers. SOC2 evidence is a gating item for Dedicated contract. Security questionnaire uploaded to Drive.

Commercial / procurement:
- Procurement engaged 2026-03-02. Looking for reserved capacity pricing for 3x current average QPS with burstability. Procurement asks for SLA language on latency and uptime; legal to review Redwood MSA.

Quotes from stakeholders:
- CTO Evan Castillo: "We need prompt parity — small regressions cascade in product. If confusions persist, we keep the incumbent."
- Head of Product Lina Ortega: "30% savings is the goal, but not at the expense of user-facing quality."
